source.title: Narrative Lookahead in LLMs: Event-Level Decodability, Predictive Advantage, and Steering
source.authors: Donghoon Jung; Min Kim; Seo-Rin Choi; Songeun Chae; Seohyon Jung

record.tranche_reason: Conceptually tests future information and intervention in generation, but measures future narrative-event attributes rather than future tokens or rhyme words. Its results therefore do not directly test any listed version.
record.gate_note: The paper measures event-type decodability at event ends and the effects of sustained steering on later event composition. Those are related to, but distinct from, token-level prediction and rhyme planning. Cited results about future-token and rhyme work are not this study's results. Intermediate horizon-by-model values are not all reproduced as rows; selected endpoints and the paper's explicit aggregate horizon conclusions are recorded.
record.test_reason: In a new setting (open-ended story generation in four open-weight models), the study reports its own results on internal look-ahead. Hidden states predict the types of not-yet-written narrative events several events ahead, beat matched text-only predictors for the next event, and a probe-derived direction reshapes later event composition in OLMo. This bears on V5 (look-ahead beyond verse). It does not bear on token-level V2, rhyme V1/V4, pre-caching V3, or token-horizon V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Accurate. The authors also state that decodability may reflect broad narrative constraints, not a dedicated planning computation (they cite pre-caching vs breadcrumbs).
record.recipe_differences: Uses narrative event-type labels and event-end hidden states rather than future-token decoding; adds matched-prefix text predictors and sustained probe-direction steering. It does not reproduce the original token-level or rhyme intervention methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Predictive advantage over text is reported only at h=1. Steering outcome differs by model and strength: OLMo meets the bidirectional criterion at k=16 and 32; Gemma does not under the tested protocol and both directions lower SOCIAL scores at higher strengths. Stronger OLMo steering has generation-quality costs.
record.problems: One minimal English prompt and one sampling temperature across four 24–32B instruction-tuned models; generalization to other prompts, genres, scales, or human-authored narratives is untested. Event extraction and labels come from a proprietary LLM and human validation covers only 30 OLMo stories; steered outputs were not separately human-validated. Text comparison uses two primary representations and linear readouts, and the authors note stronger text predictors remain to be evaluated. Steering is sustained at one selected layer and changes aggregate composition, not a localized event-boundary causal role or naturally operative planning. The Gemma steering pilot has 30 stories per condition; OLMo's main 100-seed experiment includes all 30 pilot seeds. Steering has quality costs at high strengths.
record.rows_left_out: Not all intermediate horizon-specific probing and text-comparison entries in Tables 8–11 are individually represented; the retained rows include h=1, each model's furthest reported Holm-significant prevalence horizon, and the explicit aggregate conclusion for text advantage at h≥2. Other steering strengths, pilot OLMo contrasts, and supplementary event-count, attribute, and quality diagnostics in Appendices E and G are omitted; the main bidirectional OLMo strengths, random-direction controls, and Gemma's reported reversed pilot outcomes are retained.

untested.parts: Multi-step reasoning, chess, Sokoban, and non-transformer architectures. No localized test at an event boundary of whether look-ahead steers unperturbed generation.

missing.what: Off-target effects: SOCIAL steering also shifts INTERNAL (−16.09 pp) and WORLD-STATE (−24.46 pp) at k=32. This shows steering is not selective.
OLMo lower strengths: bidirectional criterion not met at k=4 (both p=.055). At k=8 only negative steering passes.

record.verdict_notes: The reader marked relation 'tests' while listing every version as not tested, which is inconsistent. I link the study to V5 as a new-setting (T3) test, because look-ahead here is measured over narrative events in story generation. Horizons count events (hundreds of tokens each), so the study does not bear on token-scale V2 or V6.

versions.untested_parts: No rhyme-word representations, rhyming-verse generation, or interventions changing a rhyme ending.
Predicts narrative event-type labels, not tokens several positions ahead from a single hidden state.

Does not test whether representations are computed because they help later positions rather than as a byproduct of next-token prediction; sustained, deliberately induced steering does not establish this.
No rhyme-planning test in open-weight models and no open attribution-graph or rhyme-specific probing tool.
Tests story generation only, not multi-step reasoning, chess, Sokoban, or other tasks and architectures.

Horizon is counted in annotated events, not tokens. The study does not establish that apparent plans are limited to a few tokens, or test whether local next-token features or heuristics explain the results.

relationships.condition: Story generation, four 24–32B open models, next-event and multi-event decodability
relationships.reason: Event types are decodable above prevalence 4–9 events ahead (R1–R8), and beat text-only predictors at h=1 in all four models (R9–R12).
relationships.display_finding: Event types were decodable above prevalence baselines 4–9 events ahead, and activation probes outperformed predictors using generated text for the next event in all four models.

source_check.reason: R1–R12 show future-event decodability above prevalence and significant next-event superiority over both primary text predictors in all four models.

relationships.reason: No advantage over text predictors beyond the next event (R13), so farther decodability may come from the observed prefix.
relationships.display_finding: Activation probes offered no advantage over predictors using generated text beyond the next event, leaving longer-range decodability explainable by the observed prefix.

relationships.reason: A probe direction shifts the SOCIAL proportion bidirectionally (R14–R17), with the intended signs also holding against the random direction.

relation.reason: The study directly measures prospective event information and intervention effects on subsequent narrative composition.

tranche.reason: Open-ended narrative generation is a new setting with original event-level probing, matched-text comparisons and steering results bearing on V5.

source_check.notes: Sustained steering does not establish localized causal planning during unperturbed generation. All 30 OLMo pilot seeds recur in the 100-seed experiment; the single random control also changes behavior.

statements.correction: Table 6: OLMo activation .701, larger primary text .611, recent-context text .622; Qwen activation .643, larger primary text .602, recent-context text .609. Corrected significant superiority is established against both primary predictors. Other cited results match.
statements.problem: The cited scores are correct for the primary text predictors, but these are not the best evaluated text-only predictors for OLMo or Qwen.

statements.correction: Probes predict three attributes of a particular not-yet-started event at each horizon. No h≥2 meets the positive, significant superiority criterion against both primary text predictors. Sustained steering measures aggregate event composition.
statements.problem: Grouping this study's decoded event types with global response attributes misstates its prediction target; the absence of an advantage beyond h=1 is statistical and baseline-specific.
